cards.term: When Washington went to the forks of the Ohio
cards.def: In 1754 Washington led 200 Virginia militia to the Ohio forks, starting the war.

cards.term: Span of the Seven Years' War
cards.def: The war actually lasted nine years, from 1754 to 1763.
Braddock was ambushed and killed in 1755.
Louisbourg fell to the British in July 1758.
Wolfe took Quebec in 1759.
Montreal surrendered in 1760, ending the war in North America.

cards.term: When the Treaty of Paris ended the Seven Years' War
cards.def: The Treaty of Paris was signed in February 1763.
Pontiac's attacks on British forts began in summer 1763 and faded by fall 1764.
The British national debt doubled from 1754 to 1764.
The Sugar Act passed in April 1764, cutting the molasses duty from 6 to 3 pence a gallon.
The Stamp Act passed in March 1765 and took effect November 1, 1765.

cards.term: When the Stamp Act was repealed
cards.def: Parliament repealed the Stamp Act in March 1766, along with passing the Declaratory Act.
The Townshend Acts passed in 1767.
On March 5, 1770, soldiers fired into a crowd, hitting 11 and killing 5.

cards.term: When the Townshend duties were repealed
cards.def: In 1770 Lord North repealed every Townshend duty except the one on tea.
Rhode Islanders burned the Gaspee in 1772.

cards.term: When the Boston Tea Party happened
cards.def: On December 16, 1773, about 50 men dumped 90,000 pounds of tea worth £10,000.

cards.term: When the Coercive and Quebec Acts passed
cards.def: Both passed in 1774.

cards.term: When the First Continental Congress met
cards.def: In September 1774, 55 delegates from every colony but Georgia met in Philadelphia.
The fighting began on April 19, 1775, after Revere's ride on the night of April 18.
Common Sense was published in January 1776 and sold 120,000 copies.
